newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen,Nat Power up on windfall tax hopes.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen,Nat Power up on windfall tax hopes.

text.p: Shares in PowerGen Plc and National Power Plc spiked higher on Thursday as hopes that Labour's planned windfall tax would be less harsh than some previously expected swept through utility stocks, dealers said.

The two power generators were dragged higher by the water sector, which bounced after a "buy" recommendation from Schroder Securities and after press reports suggested Labour may raise less than some feared from its planned tax.
"It is just follow-through from the comments on the windfall tax," said one market-maker in electricity stocks, while others said the Schroder recommendation had spilled over into power stocks.
PowerGen was up 18p at 629-1/2 by 1103 GMT in modest volume of 488,267 shares and National Power was up 14p at 528-1/2 in volume of 4.1 million shares.
In the water sector, United Utilities Plc was up 24p at 667-1/2, Severn Trent Plc was up 22-1/2 at 741-1/2, Thames Water Plc was up 11p at 682 and Yorkshire Water Plc was up 11p at 365.

Earlier a report in the Financial Times said the opposition Labour Party, likely to win an election to be held on May 1, was still undecided on how much money would be raised from the windfall tax on privatised utilities.
The tax is planned to fund a programme of training and job-creation schemes.
The FT said Labour leader Tony Blair wanted to limit the overall amount raised to between three billion stg and five billion, less than had been sought by prospective finance minister Gordon Brown.

Brown said on Thursday that it would not decide how much to raise from the tax until after it is in power. "It will be decided after listening to the interested parties putting their views," he said at a press conference.
Separately a report in the Times newspaper on how the tax would be set concluded that Labour could spread the tax more thinly across a wide range of companies.
